title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68) that compares ungated LLM generation to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Generation used gpt-5-mini with one shared candidate per intent. The guarded arm ran a deterministic validator and applied at most one deterministic, rule-based repair when the violation type was repairable. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline emulator-executable successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (binomial) on discordant counts yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The realized near-ceiling baseline excludes the preregistered 15-percentage-point target. We provide concise, artifact-grounded descriptions of the deterministic validator, the deterministic repair operator and its invocation rule, execution accounting (400 episodes completed, hosted-model calls used = 201), the exact inferential implementation, and operational limitations. All prompts, traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution and analysis bundles referenced in the evidence manifest.

sections.introduction: Automating network operations (NetOps) with generative LLMs can increase efficiency but risks producing syntactically plausible yet operationally unsafe or incomplete configurations (incorrect ordering, missing prerequisites, protected-interface violations). Prior work has shown LLMs applied to intent-to-configuration translation and co-pilot assistance while reporting hallucinations and schema violations as recurring failure modes; mitigation proposals include verifier-assisted architectures, constrained decoding, and iterative repair. However, there is limited end-to-end, execution-grounded evidence that isolates the marginal efficacy of deterministic, auditable repairs applied to the same initial LLM candidate. We preregistered a narrowly scoped paired experiment to answer the research question stated in the preregistration: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and bounded deterministic repair (≤1 iteration) yield a higher emulator-executable configuration success rate than ungated LLM generation when both arms receive the same initial LLM candidate? Our principal contributions are: (1) a preregistered, autonomy-locked paired evaluation (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) under a shared-initial-generation estimand; (2) artifact-backed exact paired counts together with an explicit small-discordant-count inferential implementation; and (3) a concise, reproducible description of the deterministic validator and a deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline, plus concrete execution accounting and operational interpretation.
sections.related_work: Prior surveys and prototypes document active LLM use in NetOps tasks, while highlighting hallucination and structural/semantic output failures that impair safe execution. Cross-domain mitigations shown to reduce structured-output errors include retrieval-augmented generation, live schema grounding, constrained decoding, and verifier-assisted repair loops. Formal verification approaches (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) can detect reachability and isolation violations but face fidelity and scalability trade-offs when modelling dynamic control-plane behavior. Agentic-NetOps and AIOps literature emphasizes that operational reliability depends on surrounding assurance machinery (auditable traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies) in addition to base LLM capability. Our work complements these lines by measuring, under a tightly specified estimand, whether deterministic repairs applied to the same LLM candidate produce a measurable increase in emulator-executable outcomes.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental design: The experimental plan was frozen before execution (preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd...). We implemented a paired, shared-initial-generation design with n=200 confirmatory natural-language NetOps intents curated to span single-device and small cross-device changes (ACLs, VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns). Each intent produced one initial candidate via a shared LLM call; both arms used the same candidate. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory sample size (n=200) and power calculations were chosen to detect an absolute paired improvement of 15 percentage points under a conservative baseline assumption (~0.50). Model and budget: declared model gpt-5-mini; maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized hosted-model calls used = 201 (shared_initial_generation=200, repair-stage calls=1). Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet + FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator deterministically parsed, checked, and simulated candidate application.
sections.results: Execution accounting and raw outcomes: The run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) without provider/API failures. Artifact-backed primary counts: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Provider-call accounting recorded hosted-model calls used = 201 and stage_counts shared_initial_generation=200 and repair=1. Failure and repair accounting: validator-detected failures before repair (validation_before.valid == false) occurred in exactly one confirmatory episode; syntactic parse failures = 0; deterministic repair invocations = 1 (the only repair eligible under the prescribed deterministic repair-family rules). That single repair converted the failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration yielding the sole guarded-only success in the contingency table. Statistical inference: the preregistered primary test was McNemar’s test for paired binary outcomes implemented in its exact (binomial) formulation appropriate for small discordant counts. Under the exact McNemar (binomial) formulation the number of discordant pairs in one direction follows Binomial(n = n10 + n01, p = 0.5) under the null of equal marginal pass probabilities; the two-sided p-value equals the two-sided binomial tail probability for the observed ordering. With observed discordant counts n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 (n = 1), the exact two-sided binomial p-value equals 1.0. Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap seed 1729) yielding [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 target effect assumed a baseline ≈0.50; the observed near-ceiling baseline materially reduces power to detect large absolute gains and explains why the preregistered alternative is excluded by the observed CI.
sections.discussion: Interpretation within the shared-candidate estimand: Under the chosen estimand, which isolates whether a deterministic repair operator can correct the same LLM candidate deemed invalid by the validator, ungated gpt-5-mini generation already produced near-perfect candidates for the curated confirmatory distribution (199/200). Bounded deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded a marginal operational improvement (one additional pass). This narrow result does not evaluate architectures that permit independent re-sampling per arm, multi-step LLM-invoked repairs, or human-in-the-loop escalation policies; such designs increase model calls and governance complexity but may yield larger operational gains in harder or adversarial distributions. Operational takeaway: deterministic validators function as essential assurance gates—preventing execution of invalid candidates and emitting structured violation codes that enable prioritized human review or automated deterministic repair. Where baseline LLM quality is lower or the intent distribution is more adversarial, verifier-assisted strategies that allow additional LLM calls or staged repair budgets are likely to be more impactful than the bounded repair-on-same-candidate studied here.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment that evaluated whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success when both arms receive the same LLM candidate. Artifact-backed counts show baseline successes = 199/200 and guarded successes = 200/200, with paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]). The preregistered 15-percentage-point target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. For the studied estimand and distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain; practitioners should nonetheless retain deterministic validators as assurance gates and consider estimand and repair-budget trade-offs (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling; bounded rule-based repair vs LLM-invoked repair) in operational designs. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling designs, multi-vendor CLI diversity, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and higher-fidelity control-plane emulation to better characterize when GVR guards yield substantive operational benefits.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model 'gpt-5-mini'); validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' are recorded in scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; provider-call stage_counts record shared_initial_generation=200 and repair=1. All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Per-task difficulty metadata for the full confirmatory set are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; representative_artifact_hash recorded in the execution manifest). The manifest is available in the evidence bundle for per-task inspection; the present manuscript reports representative exemplars and aggregated artifact-backed counts in Table 1 rather than reproducing the full manifest listing inline.
